title: Java News Roundup: JDK 27-RC1, OpenJDK JEPs, Jakarta EE, BellSoft, Helidon, Micrometer, Tika 4.0
gist: JDK 27 has hit its first release candidate with GA scheduled for September 15, 2026, shipping post-quantum TLS key exchange, G1 as default GC everywhere, and compact object headers by default, while JDK 28 targets a built-in JSON API and deprecation of the macOS/x64 port. Downstream, Apache Tika 4.0 adds LLM inference modules (Claude, Gemini, OpenAI) and Jakarta EE pushes an Agentic AI 1.0 spec, showing AI capabilities being absorbed into core enterprise Java plumbing.

themes.theme: JDK 27 release candidate and GA feature set

insights.claim: JDK 27 formally entered its first release candidate (Build 35, zero unresolved P1 bugs) with GA scheduled for September 15, 2026, per Oracle Chief Architect Mark Reinhold.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A firm mid-September GA date anchors upgrade cycles for enterprise Java vendors and downstream JDK distributors (Azul, BellSoft, Red Hat).
insights.quote: formally declared that JDK 27 has entered its first release candidate as there are no unresolved P1 bugs in Build 35
insights.locator: As per the JDK 27 release schedule

insights.claim: JDK 27 will ship JEP 527, Post-Quantum Hybrid Key Exchange for TLS 1.3, putting post-quantum cryptography into the default Java platform used across enterprise infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Post-quantum readiness is becoming a compliance checkbox; platform-level support in Java accelerates enterprise PQC migration and pressures security vendors selling bolt-on solutions.

insights.claim: JDK 27 makes G1 the default garbage collector in all environments (JEP 523) and enables compact object headers by default (JEP 534), delivering memory-footprint and performance gains without code changes.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Default-on memory efficiency reduces cloud compute bills for Java-heavy fleets — marginal negative for cloud-spend growth, positive for Java's competitiveness in cost-sensitive workloads.

insights.claim: Structured Concurrency reaches its seventh preview and the Vector API its twelfth incubator round in JDK 27, signaling these flagship performance features remain unfinalized after years of iteration.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Long incubation cycles mean production adoption of Java's SIMD and concurrency modernization is still deferred — relevant for timing bets on JVM performance parity with native stacks.

themes.theme: JDK 28 direction: platform pruning and built-in JSON

insights.claim: JEP 541 targets JDK 28 to deprecate the macOS/x64 port for removal because Apple no longer supports the architecture, following the same maintenance-cost logic as the Windows 32-bit x86 deprecation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Confirms Apple Silicon's total displacement of Intel Macs in the dev toolchain; legacy x64 Mac fleets lose runtime support paths.
insights.quote: the intent to remove this port in a future release to save on maintenance costs

insights.claim: JEP 540 targets JDK 28 with a standard incubating JSON API (implementing RFC 8259), removing the need for external libraries like Jackson or Gson for basic JSON parsing and generation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Platform absorption of a ubiquitous third-party dependency shrinks the surface area (and supply-chain risk) of the Java ecosystem's most common library category — watch impact on Jackson-dependent tooling vendors.
insights.quote: defines a simple, standard API for parsing and generating JSON documents without the need for an external library

insights.claim: JEP 542 proposes finalizing PEM encodings of cryptographic objects in JDK 28 after three preview rounds (JDK 25-27), with the review concluding August 26, 2026 and a rename of DEREncodable to BinaryEncodable.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Standardized certificate/key handling in the JDK reduces dependence on Bouncy Castle-style crypto libraries for common PKI workflows.

themes.theme: AI absorbed into enterprise Java plumbing

insights.claim: Apache Tika 4.0.0 GA ships new inference and OCR modules supporting Claude, Gemini, OpenAI and Tesseract, embedding commercial LLM connectors directly into the standard open-source document-extraction toolkit.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Document-AI is commoditizing: when free infrastructure like Tika bundles multi-vendor LLM inference, standalone document-parsing startups lose differentiation while LLM API providers gain a distribution channel.
insights.quote: new inference and OCR modules that support Claude, Gemini, OpenAI and Tesseract OCR

insights.claim: Tika 4.0 adds a MarkdownParser producing structured lossless XHTML and moves document parsing into its own forked process, alongside a migration from XML to JSON configuration — breaking changes aimed at LLM-era pipelines and isolation.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Markdown-first, process-isolated parsing is the shape RAG ingestion pipelines demand; Tika is repositioning as RAG infrastructure.

insights.claim: The Jakarta Agentic AI 1.0 specification, approved in early November 2025, has delivered its first milestone (M1) release, meaning agentic AI is being standardized at the enterprise Java specification level.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A vendor-neutral agentic-AI spec in Jakarta EE would pull enterprise agent workloads toward standardized Java stacks rather than proprietary frameworks — early but worth tracking for the enterprise-AI middleware trade.

insights.claim: Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile is on track to release in time for JakartaOne Livestream 2026, with the Web Profile and full Platform targeted for the first half of 2027, per Eclipse Foundation developer advocate Ivar Grimstad.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Sets the upgrade cadence for the enterprise Java app-server ecosystem (WildFly, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Payara) into 2027.
insights.quote: The goal of releasing Jakarta EE 12 Core Profile in time for JakartaOne Livestream 2026 seems to be on track.
insights.locator: In his weekly Hashtag Jakarta EE

insights.claim: BellSoft shipped Critical Security Patch updates across eight Liberica JDK versions (from JDK 26 down to 6u513) concurrent with Oracle's August 2026 CSPU, totaling 29 fixes and backports with BellSoft contributing to eliminating 11 issues.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Downstream JDK vendors matching Oracle's patch cadence — including for Java 6/7-era runtimes — shows the long-tail support market monetizing legacy enterprise Java; a moat for Oracle alternatives like BellSoft and Azul.

insights.claim: Helidon 4.5.3 now requires authentication configuration for Long Running Actions participant callbacks and caps JSON processing at 1000 nested structures — defensive hardening against callback abuse and JSON-based DoS.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Framework maintainers are proactively closing deeply-nested-payload and unauthenticated-callback attack classes; consistent with rising API-abuse threat activity.

insights.claim: Micrometer Tracing 1.8.0-M1 refactored its W3CPropagation class specifically to harden against malicious injections, denial-of-service attacks and OutOfMemory exceptions, treating trace-context headers as an attack surface.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Observability plumbing itself is now recognized as an injection/DoS vector — a data point for the growing observability-security convergence theme.
insights.quote: improved security against malicious injections, denial of service attacks and OutOfMemory exceptions
insights.locator: The first milestone release of Micrometer Tracing

insights.claim: Micrometer Metrics 1.18.0-M1 drops OpenTelemetry Protobuf definitions in favor of the OpenTelemetry Metrics SDK and OTLP Exporter with shading, and optimizes PrometheusMeterRegistry for faster metric collection.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Continued consolidation of the Java observability stack onto OpenTelemetry standards — reinforces OTel as the de facto telemetry protocol layer that commercial observability vendors must interoperate with.
insights.locator: The first milestone release of Micrometer Metrics
